list.description: Prometheus scraping the TON node metrics exporters
list.label: Prometheus
list.name: datasource
job
list.label: job
list.description: The scrape job to look at: one job is one network. Single-select on purpose — chain-level panels sum seqnos, block rates and collation budgets across whatever the selector spans, so a multi-job selection would merge unrelated fleets (mainnet + testnet) into one meaningless chain. Compare networks in two tabs.

list.name: instance
list.label: instance
list.description: Node filter within the selected job. Node and fleet-diagnostic panels respect it; chain-truth panels explicitly query every reporter in the job so selecting one node cannot redefine the blockchain.

list.name: agg
list.label: Node aggregation
list.description: How per-class and per-operation panels collapse selected nodes that expose the series: worst = maximum, p95 = the 95th percentile, median = the typical node, and best = minimum. Time-per-item panels include only nodes with traffic, where the ratio is defined. Health and tail panels keep their fixed aggregation. A ▾ in the title marks panels controlled by this selector.

list.name: scope
list.label: scope
list.description: Metric-scope filter: which exporter scope the transport series are read from. Nodes report their own scope values, so a fleet mid-rollout can expose more than one.

list.name: trust
list.label: QUIC peer class
list.description: Filters peer-attributable QUIC app, query, delivery, and ready-connection metrics. The wire/app overhead ratio remains all-peers so its app denominator matches the unsplit wire numerator. Socket/pre-auth QUIC and all ADNL, RLDP2, and overlay series also remain all-peers. Pre-trust builds expose no trust label: their QUIC series appear under All, but not under trusted or untrusted.

panels.title: UDP in (fleet)

targets.expr: sum(label_replace(rate(ton_adnl_wire_bytes_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",direction="in"}[$__rate_interval]), "transport", "adnl", "", "") or label_replace(rate(ton_quic_wire_bytes_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",direction="in"}[$__rate_interval]), "transport", "quic", "", ""))

panels.description: UDP payload bytes/s the sockets received, summed over ADNL and QUIC for all selected nodes. RLDP2 rides inside ADNL and is already counted there. Informational; no health threshold.

panels.title: UDP out (fleet)

targets.expr: sum(label_replace(rate(ton_adnl_wire_bytes_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",direction="out"}[$__rate_interval]), "transport", "adnl", "", "") or label_replace(rate(ton_quic_wire_bytes_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",direction="out"}[$__rate_interval]), "transport", "quic", "", ""))

panels.description: UDP payload bytes/s the kernel accepted for sending, summed over ADNL and QUIC for all selected nodes. Refused sends are drops, not wire traffic. Informational; no health threshold.

panels.title: QUIC query RTT p95

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(ton_quic_query_roundtrip_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",trust=~"$trust"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: Outbound QUIC query roundtrip p95 for the selected peer class, computed from histogram buckets summed across the fleet. Includes network path, peer processing, and transfer time. Yellow at 0.5 s; red at 2 s.

panels.title: QUIC query fail %

targets.expr: sum(rate(ton_quic_query_roundtrip_failed_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",trust=~"$trust"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(ton_quic_query_roundtrip_seconds_count{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",trust=~"$trust"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.description: Outbound QUIC query failures divided by measured roundtrips for the selected peer class across the fleet. Green below 1%, yellow at 1%, red at 5%. No data means no completed QUIC queries in the interval; it is not presented as a healthy 0%.

panels.title: QUIC packet loss %

targets.expr: sum(rate(ton_quic_transport_packets_lost_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(ton_quic_transport_packets_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",direction="out"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.description: QUIC packets declared lost divided by outbound packets across the fleet. Most loss is recovered, but it costs bandwidth and tail latency. Yellow at 1%; red at 5%. No outbound packets in the current interval renders No data, not 0%.

panels.title: Kernel RX overflow (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, sum by (job, instance) (label_replace(rate(ton_quic_wire_dropped_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",direction="in",reason="limited"}[$__rate_interval]), "transport", "quic", "", "") or label_replace(rate(ton_adnl_wire_dropped_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",ton_scope=~"$scope",direction="in",reason="limited"}[$__rate_interval]), "transport", "adnl", "", "")))

panels.description: Worst-node ADNL + QUIC datagrams/s dropped because a socket receive buffer was full (SO_RXQ_OVFL). Sustained nonzero means ingress outruns the reader; raise SO_RCVBUF or add read capacity, then inspect the by-node panel. Linux-only: macOS/local nets report structural zero, meaning no signal rather than proof of no drops. The tile names the worst node.

panels.description: ▾ Transport-accept to answer for queries we send: network + peer processing + transfer time. The p95 is each node's own; the Node switch collapses across nodes, so worst asks 'is RTT bad everywhere or on one node' and the hover row names it. QUIC is split by peer class; ADNL remains all-peers. RLDP2 bulk-transfer latency is separate below because it is not comparable with low-latency ADNL/QUIC. Hover attribution: the tooltip lists "series ⇒ node" rows (hidden from the chart) answering, per series, whose number the drawn line is. Each row names one stable node for the visible range — on a Node-switch panel the node whose series stays nearest the drawn quantile (the dominant node under worst, the node the median follows under median), elsewhere the node that dominated the range — and always carries that node's own value, so where the row hugs the drawn line, the line is that node.
